newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end upbeat, high on Wall St rush.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end upbeat, high on Wall St rush.

text.p: French shares ran up solid gains on Friday, emboldened by bonds which welcomed weak U.S. September employment figures, traders said. The market had been drifting in negative ground before the U.S. data.
Strength on Wall Street and the London FTSE back above the 4,000 at record levels lent powerful support.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 16.60 points or 0.78 percent at 2,152.69, and was up 2.17 percent on the week.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up 19 points at 2,159 from Thursday's close.
* The surprise 40,000 fall in U.S. unemployment assuaged fears of Fed tightening, which propelled bond markets sky-high
* Next major target for the CAC-40 index was 2,064, one market operator said
* Blue chips and financials gained around on one percent, with Union des Assurances de Paris outperforming with a rise of 3.12 percent, adding 3.40 francs to 112.40
Societe Generale firmed 1.77 percent to 575, Cie Bancaire up 2.63 percent at 547
* Speculation on an alliance pushed up Promodes, up 1.02 percent to 1,388, and Casino, up 5.62 percent
* Eramet closed down seven francs at 303 on a report in Le Monde newspaper that chairman Yves Rambaud may have to resign if a proposed change in the nickel producer's legal status goes through.
* Lyonnaise des Eaux recovers some ground lost over the week since it reported disappointing H1 results.

The company made a presentation to fund managers in London on Friday which contained substantial changes in emphasis from an analysts meeting in Paris the previous week, a market source said. It stressed the return on capital employed in its divisions and its strength as a services company.
* Bouygues firms 0.66 percent to 472 francs ahead of its first-half results next Tuesday.
One analyst said he expects virtually flat earnings growth, though this should not concern the market as the first half is not representative for the year, due to the winter slowdown.
* The company's mobile telephone activities, launched in the summer, a market focus.
* Eurotunnel discloses details of its debt restructuring on Monday at 1030 GMT. The shares are expected to requote on Tuesday morning.
* Two blocks of Publicis stock changed hands, 100,000 and 77,000 at respectively 435 and 440 francs. The shares ended down five at 440.
